summary:
We developed Lunar Navigator, a web-based platform that evaluates landing sites at the Moon's south pole and analyses mission feasibility. It brings together the key factors in site selection, such as terrain slope, surface roughness, sunlight availability, and proximity to permanently shadowed regions, into one interactive tool. Instead of studying scattered datasets by hand, mission planners can compare candidate sites side by side and see which are safest and most valuable.
The south pole is one of the hardest places to land. Extreme lighting, long shadows, and rugged terrain make landings risky, and a poor choice can cost an entire mission. Our solution addresses this by turning complex lunar data into clear, comparable site assessments, helping teams make faster and better-informed decisions about where to land and how to plan the mission.
This matters because the lunar south pole is the focus of the next generation of exploration. Its shadowed craters are believed to hold water ice, which could support future life support, fuel production, and long-term lunar bases. Safer landing site selection reduces mission risk and cost, and supports India's growing space ambitions and global exploration efforts.

What it does and how it works
Lunar Navigator is a web-based tool that evaluates landing sites at the Moon’s south pole and analyses mission feasibility. Users explore candidate sites and compare them on factors such as slope, terrain roughness, sunlight and shadow, [Earth communication visibility], and distance to permanently shadowed regions that may hold water ice. The tool turns these factors into clear, comparable site assessments, so planners can quickly see which locations are safest and most valuable. [Add whether it uses scoring, a map view, or charts.]

Benefits

  • Saves time by putting scattered lunar data into one interface
  • Makes site comparison clear and consistent instead of manual
  • Reduces landing risk by highlighting hazardous terrain and poor lighting
  • Easy to use, since it runs in a browser with nothing to install

Intended impact
We want to support safer, better-informed landing decisions for south pole missions. Those missions matter because lunar water ice could support life support, fuel production, and future lunar bases. We also hope it helps students, researchers, and space enthusiasts understand how landing sites are chosen.

Tools and technologies

  • Built with Google AI Studio [and Gemini, if you used it for analysis or code generation]

How it is creative
Most lunar site analysis happens in specialist tools or research papers. We made it accessible and interactive by combining several landing factors into one view, so even non-experts can understand why one site is better than another. [Add any unique feature, such as AI-generated explanations, 3D view, or a custom scoring method.]

Factors the team considered

  • Technical: slope, roughness, illumination, communication line-of-sight, and proximity to water ice
  • Mission: landing safety, power availability, and resource access
  • Practical: ease of use, clarity of results, and reliable data sources
  • Future potential: scalability to more sites and additional data layer
